question.text: When assessing a client's financial position, the investment adviser should consider which of the following as 'income'?

answer.text: Only the client's salary or business income
All sources including salary, rental income, interest income, dividends, and any other regular or irregular receipts
Only taxable income as declared in the ITR
Only income from employment and investments, excluding gifts or inheritances

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series X-A captures income broadly. Page 18 notes that income can arise from profession, salary, business or investments. Pages 48, 54 and 57 describe annual income as covering employment or business income together with interest, dividend, rent and similar receipts. Capturing all of these is essential for a complete cash-flow picture. The Trap: Limiting income to salary alone or to ITR-declared figures excludes investment and rental cash flows that the source explicitly lists. Excluding all non-employment/non-investment items also understates household resources whenever interest, dividend or rent receipts are material. Note: The income heads above (salary, profession, business, investments, interest, dividend, rent) are drawn directly from pages 18, 48, 54 and 57 of NISM Series X-A.
